artworks.title: Hippomenes and Atalanta
artworks.description: Reni's Prado canvas freezes the race's hinge: Atalanta stoops for a golden apple while Hippomenes surges ahead — Aphrodite's gift buying victory.

artworks.title: The Race between Hippomenes and Atalanta
artworks.description: Hallé's Louvre Rococo race: Atalanta hesitates over scattered apples as Hippomenes runs on — Ovid's contest as courtly allegory of love conquering pride.

artworks.title: Atalanta and Hippomenes
artworks.description: Colombel's late-Baroque runners restage the footrace — the huntress who races suitors to the death, slowed by gold that will cost them both.

artworks.title: Atalanta and Hippomenes, from 'Game of Mythology'
artworks.description: MET engraving from the Jeu de la Mythologie: the race reduced to a playing-card emblem — golden apples and the suitor who will not be outrun.

music.title: Atalanta
music.description: Handel's pastoral for Frederick, Prince of Wales, casts Atalanta as a huntress of love and flight — the Arcadian runner on the London stage.

popCulture.title: Atalanta
popCulture.description: The huntress who races suitors to the death — Hippomenes' golden apples remain the myth of desire buying victory.
